messages:
devon: FYI customer "ACME Health" is locked down behind a corporate outbound proxy + strict allowlist. They want a single short list of IPs/CIDRs to allow for our edge endpoints and healthchecks. Any volunteers to draft guidance?

maria: Short version: give them stable FQDNs + our published CIDR bundle. But customers often insist on IPs. We should also call out SNAT port exhaustion and healthcheck source IP behavior.

sre_jake: +1. Important to note: depending on deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated) source IPs differ. Hosted -> we publish a relatively small set of egress IPs; Dedicated -> per-customer NAT ranges. Need to ask which they mean.

tim: Quick checklist to send them: ports 443 outbound, 53 UDP/TCP for DNS (if they do internal DNS), TLS SNI for healthchecks works for customers that allow domain names. If they require IPs, provide the CIDR file and a fallback: allow healthcheck FQDN.

olga: Customer replied: "we can only do IPs, no DNS or FQDNs allowed due to compliance." They asked for a signed attestation that IPs won't change more than monthly. We can't commit a hard SLA on IP rotation but can offer a 30-day heads-up and an IP bundle URL they can fetch.

sre_jake: Concrete proposal to share with them (short):

- allow outbound TCP 443 to: 203.0.113.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, 198.51.101.0/25
- allow outbound TCP 80 to same cidrs (health fallbacks)
- allow outbound UDP 53 and TCP 53 to any internal resolver (or our IPs if they proxy DNS)
- allow our healthcheck host: health.edge.redwood-inference.com (if DNS allowed)

Also include guidance: "If you SNAT/masquerade at your proxy, ensure ephemeral ports aren't exhausted — recommend port range >= 1024-65535 and enable connection reuse."

maria: Add these operational notes to the message: retry/backoff recommendations (5s jittered, exponential, max 3 attempts) and link to our /ip-bundle endpoint so they can pull the list programmatically.

devon: I'll paste a curl snippet for their ops team to test connectivity and SNI.

devon: ```
# test TLS SNI + Host header against health endpoint
curl -v --resolve "health.edge.redwood-inference.com:443:203.0.113.5" \
  https://health.edge.redwood-inference.com/healthz -H "Host: health.edge.redwood-inference.com"
```

tim: Nice. Also tell them about potential hairpin issues if they try to route traffic back through the same corporate proxy — some proxies rewrite TLS or do TLS-inspection that will break health checks. Suggest a passthrough rule for TLS on that destination IP range.

egress-bot: NOTE: current published edge egress bundle (canonical) -> https://status.redwood-inference.com/egress-ips.json (expires in 30 days). Fields: ["cidrs","last_updated","rotation_window_days"].

olga: Customer asked about NAT port exhaustion mitigations. Any tips?

sre_jake: Ops tips:
- Prefer using a NAT gateway with port preservation or use a dedicated NAT pool if possible.
- Increase ephemeral port range on their proxies, enable TCP keepalive and connection pooling.
- If they run an internal proxy (squid/varnish), tune max_sockets and keepalive.
- If SNAT is unavoidable, ask for a NAT port estimate based on expected concurrent connections: estimate tokens_per_request = ~1 for long-lived streams, up to 10 for bursty short requests; multiply by concurrency to size ports.

maria: I'll turn this into a short one-page attachment for ACME with the exact cidrs and the curl tests. We should also include a note about ALB vs NLB: NLB preserves client source IP -> useful for customers that want to filter by source IP; ALB will SNAT.

devon: Great. I'll draft the text and include the below sample JSON they can poll:

```json
{
  "cidrs": ["203.0.113.0/24", "198.51.100.0/24", "198.51.101.0/25"],
  "last_updated": "2026-03-12T16:00:00Z",
  "rotation_window_days": "30"
}
```

tim: One more callout — for customers using on-prem proxies that do full TLS interception, request a passthrough for the health host or set up an allowlist for our proxy user-agent to avoid false positives in health dashboards.

olga: I'll send the doc to the customer and follow up if they push back on the IP set. Thanks everyone :+1:

sre_jake: If they do push back, we can propose a VPN peering/private link option (Private mode) which removes the public egress allowlist requirement.
